datasets.name: Shadow Library
datasets.organization: Alaya Lab and Shanghai Innovation Institute
datasets.description: The unreleased ShadowDancer training corpus of synchronized shadow pairs that preserve dynamics while resampling appearance, plus real-video self-pairs for visual realism across human, robot, game, and static-scene domains.

derived_from.contribution: Roughly 0.3M static-scene self-pair frames
derived_from.notes: The paper names DL3DV as the static-scene source; no released row-level mapping is available.

derived_from.contribution: Roughly 6.5M Internet-video self-pair frames
derived_from.notes: The paper names MiraData for visual-realism self-pairs; source URL rights remain upstream-dependent.

derived_from.contribution: Roughly 3.6M frames from six selected robot datasets
derived_from.notes: BridgeData, FurnitureBench, Berkeley UR5, Jaco Play, Stanford HYDRA, and RoboTurk are named; their individual provenance and terms remain layered.

access.notes: The paper documents source families, approximate sequence and frame counts, and some mixture percentages, but publishes no files, manifest, download link, or dataset license.

scale.notes: Summing the rounded table entries yields about 20.5M frames; sequence counts, percentages, and frames are approximate and several game/render rows do not disclose final mixture percentages.

license.media: Heterogeneous simulator, rendered, game, public-dataset, and web-video rights
license.notes: CC-BY-4.0 applies to the paper, not automatically to the unreleased corpus; simulator and game assets plus public-source licenses require component-level review.

known_limitations: Files, manifests, duplicate reports, filters, and per-sample provenance are unavailable for independent audit.
Self-pairs preserve appearance as well as motion and therefore teach visual realism differently from synthetic cross-shadow pairs.
Approximate table counts and incomplete mixture percentages do not establish the final optimization sampling distribution.
Game and simulator coverage may overrepresent controllable, repeatable dynamics relative to noisy real-world interaction.

processing.recipe: Replay identical dynamics under independently resampled character, scene, lighting, and camera conditions where engines permit; pair public real videos with themselves; then sample source families for cross-shadow prediction and block-causal rollout training.
processing.notes: If released, retain paired-frame alignment, source family, exact upstream item ID, resampled factors, control mask, license, and takedown state.

datasets.name: ReMind1M
datasets.description: A public 1,419,331-row dynamic-memory video release containing physics-filtered Helios generations, pair-fixed InSpatio camera augmentations, and Kubric camera renders with production motion-focused captions.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts 557 GB of WebDataset tar shards plus three authoritative compressed JSONL manifests; pin revision 0619eaa6455b5bdf5b6f270929fd8ab75028dd3d.

scale.notes: 1,027,329 Helios rows, 265,945 pair-fixed InSpatio rows, and 126,057 Kubric rows; use the manifests rather than inferring counts from shard numbers.

license.media: Underlying generated and simulated videos retain source and component terms
license.notes: ReMind-authored captions, audit metadata, and manifest arrangement are CC-BY-NC-4.0; the license explicitly does not relicense underlying videos or third-party metadata.

known_limitations: Generated physics and model-written captions can contain implausible motion, hallucinations, or systematic generator bias despite automated filtering.
The InSpatio release excludes depth videos and raw pipeline metadata, limiting independent geometry audits.
Only the corrected pair-fixed manifest should be used; older manifests contain an 8-by-32 shard-export transpose that can mismatch identity, caption, and trajectory.
This released subset does not include the full real-video mixture used by ReMind.

processing.recipe: Filter Helios clips for physics plausibility and sustained dynamics, pair InSpatio RGB video with corrected DA3 trajectories, remove static Kubric samples except camera tours, and scrub camera instructions from captions because control lives in pose metadata.
processing.notes: Preserve unknown manifest fields, use only train_manifest_inspatio_pairfix.jsonl.gz for InSpatio, and keep camera NPZ members paired with their MP4 identity.

datasets.name: UniGen-AR Evaluation Suite
datasets.organization: UniGen-AR authors and upstream benchmark maintainers
datasets.description: A relationship card for the six public benchmarks used by UniGen-AR: GenEval for text-to-image, Emu-Edit for image editing, NYUv2 for depth and normals, LOL for low light, GoPro for deblurring, and Rain-13K for deraining.

access.notes: There is no combined download. Use the upstream GenEval, Emu-Edit, NYUv2, LOL, GoPro, and Rain-13K project releases named by the paper and preserve their separate terms and splits.

scale.notes: The paper evaluates on each upstream benchmark's standard split and does not publish a merged record count.

license.media: Heterogeneous upstream benchmark terms
license.notes: The UniGen-AR paper's CC-BY-4.0 license does not relicense benchmark media; obtain and review every component independently.

known_limitations: The six tasks have different metrics, licenses, split protocols, and data-generating processes, so aggregate claims require per-benchmark context.
Several restoration benchmarks are small or domain-specific and do not establish robustness on open-world degradations.
This card records a reported evaluation relationship, not a redistributable merged dataset.

processing.recipe: Evaluate text-to-image on GenEval, editing on Emu-Edit, depth and normals on NYUv2, low-light enhancement on LOL, deblurring on GoPro, and deraining on Rain-13K using their standard protocols.
processing.notes: Upstream entry points are https://github.com/djghosh13/geneval, https://github.com/facebookresearch/emu, https://cs.nyu.edu/~fergus/datasets/nyu_depth_v2.html, https://daooshee.github.io/BMVC2018website/, https://seungjunnah.github.io/Datasets/gopro, and https://github.com/csdwren/PReNet.

datasets.name: InsAVE-80K
datasets.organization: Nanyang Technological University and MMLab, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
datasets.description: A paired audiovisual editing corpus with 87,074 released training pairs and 1,000 evaluation pairs spanning object insertion and removal, identity and voice cloning, and general joint audio-video edits.

derived_from.contribution: source movie clips
derived_from.notes: The paper names MovieBench among the public datasets used to source original audiovisual clips; retained counts are not disclosed.

derived_from.contribution: source movie clips
derived_from.notes: The paper names Condensed Movies among the public datasets used to source original audiovisual clips; retained counts are not disclosed.

derived_from.contribution: source short-film clips
derived_from.notes: The paper names Short-Films-20K among the public datasets used to source original audiovisual clips; retained counts are not disclosed.

derived_from.contribution: source sound-event videos
derived_from.notes: The paper names VGGSound among the public datasets used to source original audiovisual clips; retained counts are not disclosed.

access.notes: Hugging Face hosts eleven WebDataset tar shards totaling about 139 GB; pin revision 8ba8cca1917186fe21f610954af6146def52b259 and preserve the released train and eval directories.

scale.notes: Current card counts are 87,074 train plus 1,000 eval pairs and 176,148 video files; the paper's original 79K-train figure predates this larger release.

license.media: Layered upstream and original-media rights are not relicensed by the dataset card
license.notes: The Hugging Face card declares MIT but explicitly makes users responsible for permissions, licenses, and copyrights attached to underlying media.

known_limitations: Synthetic video and audio targets can retain artifacts, identity errors, hallucinated content, or imperfect audiovisual synchronization after automated filtering.
Public-web and upstream-dataset media have layered rights and incomplete retained-item provenance.
The current release has 8,074 more training pairs than the paper's 79K figure without a published version-by-version reconciliation.
Automatic quality judges and human verification of only the evaluation split do not eliminate model-specific selection bias.

processing.recipe: Segment source media, filter motion and audiovisual quality, categorize content, localize speakers and objects, generate masks and reversible instructions, synthesize or separate audio, produce edited targets, and retain pairs passing five multimodal quality criteria.
processing.notes: Preserve pair direction, category, original source identity, synthesis lineage, quality judgments, release split, shard hash, and upstream rights metadata.

datasets.name: InnoText-30K
datasets.description: A 30,000-sample English-Chinese visual-text corpus that combines Lex-10K, 10,000 synthetic Chinese counterparts, and a curated 10,000-sample AnyWord-3M subset for unified text generation and editing.

access.notes: The paper describes the corpus and InnoText-Bench, but no dataset files, metadata repository, license, or request path is linked.

scale.notes: The paper reports 20K Chinese and 10K English samples. The Chinese portion contains 10K newly synthesized samples and a selected 10K AnyWord-3M subset; InnoText-Bench contains 1,500 images sampled across the three components.

license.media: Lex-10K, AnyWord-3M, and Seedream-generated component terms require separate review
license.notes: The arXiv paper license does not license the dataset; no combined-corpus terms or upstream attribution manifest is published.

known_limitations: The release has no inspectable files, hashes, split manifest, or dataset-specific license.
Synthetic Chinese images are generated through InternVL3 prompt expansion and Seedream, so model-specific artifacts and cultural bias can propagate.
The paper evaluates aesthetics and naturalness but does not publish per-record scores or curation retention rates.

processing.recipe: recipes/image_text
processing.notes: Preserve upstream component, translation and expansion prompts, generator version, aesthetic scores, PPOCR-v4 annotations, DeepSeek-VL2 captions, language, split, and license provenance.

datasets.name: ID-V2V Poly Haven HDRI Sample

access.notes: Poly Haven assets are openly browsable, but the exact assets, revisions, sampling weights, and manifest used by ID-V2V are not published.

scale.notes: Neither the number of distinct HDRIs nor the draw count and distribution are reported.

license.media: Poly Haven assets are CC0
license.notes: Underlying Poly Haven assets are CC0, while live API or website access remains subject to platform terms; pin asset IDs and downloaded revisions.

known_limitations: Exact asset identities, revision dates, resolution choices, exposure processing, and sampling distribution are not disclosed.
Environment-map coverage may not represent ordinary indoor lighting or all geographic and cultural settings.

processing.notes: Record Poly Haven asset ID, file revision, license snapshot, resolution, exposure and rotation, download method, and every synthetic render association.

datasets.name: ID-V2V LuxPostFacto OLAT Subset
datasets.description: The exact unreleased subset of LuxPostFacto One-Light-at-a-Time facial captures from 67 participants used by ID-V2V to synthesize face-relighting training pairs.

access.notes: ID-V2V names the upstream LuxPostFacto captures but publishes neither the selected files nor an acquisition or request path.

scale.notes: The source component covers 67 participants with varied pose, expression, and camera viewpoint; image count is not stated separately.

license.media: LuxPostFacto OLAT participant captures with no dataset-level terms cited by ID-V2V
license.notes: Participant consent scope, biometric-data handling, access terms, and permission for redistribution are not documented in the ID-V2V release.

known_limitations: Exact participant selection, capture files, demographic distribution, consent scope, and rights are not published.
Static OLAT facial captures do not represent full natural video motion or the diversity of in-the-wild illumination.

processing.notes: Preserve participant consent and identity controls, camera and light indices, HDR calibration, source-session provenance, and permitted downstream uses.

datasets.name: ID-V2V Human-Centric Video Corpus
datasets.description: The unreleased 40,000-video single- and multi-subject corpus used to train ID-V2V for identity-preserving video restylization with derived face, normal, depth, keyframe, and caption controls.

access.notes: The paper provides construction details but no source list, download, manifest, request path, or dataset license.

scale.notes: Videos are trained at 1280x720 with 81 frames; the original clip durations and total hours are not reported.

license.media: Unnamed human-centric videos with undisclosed source, consent, and license terms
license.notes: The Apache-2.0 code and checkpoint license does not establish rights to the unreleased people-centered training media.

known_limitations: Source platforms, participant consent, identity privacy review, collection dates, geographic distribution, and media licenses are not disclosed.
Videos with no detected faces in more than 40% of frames are removed, which may bias toward large, frontal, and consistently visible faces.
At most five detected faces per frame are retained, so crowded multi-subject scenes receive incomplete identity controls.

processing.recipe: recipes/video_text
processing.notes: Preserve source and consent records, caption-model version, per-frame face boxes and filter decisions, relighting parameters, normals, depth, keyframes, and exact checkpoint provenance.

datasets.name: ID-V2V Face Relighting Pairs
datasets.description: Approximately 330,000 unreleased paired facial images synthesized from LuxPostFacto OLAT captures and Poly Haven HDRIs to train ID-V2V's dedicated SVD-derived face-relighting model.

derived_from.contribution: OLAT facial captures from 67 participants
derived_from.notes: Supplies facial reflectance observations across poses, expressions, viewpoints, and individual lights.

derived_from.contribution: HDR environment maps for arbitrary input illumination
derived_from.notes: Randomly sampled HDRIs illuminate the OLAT captures before construction of top-lit targets.

access.notes: The paper reports the synthesis procedure and scale but provides no paired images, manifest, generator code path, or request process.

scale.notes: About 330K input-target image pairs are rendered from 67 participants; the number of distinct HDRIs and pairs per participant are not reported.

license.media: Synthetic derivatives of restricted or undisclosed OLAT captures and CC0 Poly Haven HDRIs
license.notes: CC0 HDRI terms do not resolve consent, biometric, or redistribution rights for the participant captures and resulting face pairs.

known_limitations: Exact synthesis configurations, HDRI selection, pair distribution, participant demographics, and failure filtering are not published.
Training supervision uses a fixed top-light target that may underrepresent other ordinary illumination conditions.

processing.notes: Preserve upstream catalog IDs, participant and consent controls, OLAT and HDRI identifiers, render settings, target-light definition, pair ID, and rights metadata.

datasets.name: ID-V2V Evaluation Suite
datasets.description: Two unreleased human-centric video-restylization evaluation sets comprising 100 single-subject and 60 two-subject source videos with edited first-frame targets.

access.notes: The paper reports construction and metrics but does not release the source videos, keyframes, prompts, metadata, or request path.

scale.notes: Contains 100 single-subject and 60 two-subject videos; a separate user study samples 20 cases from each group.

license.media: Unnamed human-centric source videos and generated keyframes with undisclosed rights
license.notes: Source licenses, participant consent, Gemini and Qwen output terms, and benchmark redistribution terms are not published.

known_limitations: Source identities, selection method, demographic distribution, prompts, generated keyframes, and manual filtering criteria are unavailable.
Quantitative comparison caps subjects at two because baselines do not reliably support larger groups.

processing.notes: Preserve source rights and consent, subject-count split, Gemini proposal, Qwen-Image-Edit configuration, depth and edge conditions, manual filter decision, and metric versions.

datasets.name: fMRI-Face
datasets.description: A controlled neural-decoding dataset containing 62,856 paired fMRI and full-HD digital-human face-video samples from three consenting participants.

access.notes: The paper fully describes acquisition and splits but does not link public files, a repository, a data-use agreement, or an application process.

scale.notes: Three subjects viewed 2,174 unique 8-second, 240-frame, 30 FPS, 1920x1080 digital-human clips. Sliding 1.6-second fMRI windows yield 18,108 training and 2,844 test pairs per subject, totaling 62,856.

license.media: Digital-human assets and sensitive fMRI responses; reuse terms are not published
license.notes: Ethics approval and written informed consent are reported, but no public data license, participant-level consent scope, or redistribution protocol is available.

known_limitations: Only three participants aged 22 to 24 were scanned, limiting demographic and cross-subject generalization.
Controlled background-free digital-human stimuli differ from natural facial behavior and social context.
Brain data is sensitive personal data and should not be redistributed or re-identified without an explicit approved governance process.

processing.notes: Keep participant identifiers pseudonymized and separated, preserve ethics and consent scope, MRI acquisition and preprocessing provenance, stimulus hashes, 3D parameters, temporal alignment, and subject-safe train/test splits.

datasets.name: AgentHOI Mixed-Source Training Corpus
datasets.description: The unreleased 108,000-clip human-object-interaction corpus used by AgentHOI, combining 71,000 mined real clips with 37,000 synthetic interaction videos.

access.notes: Code and checkpoints are public, but the official repository states that training data is not included and provides no dataset request path.

scale.notes: The paper reports 71K real clips mined from 10M online videos and 37K synthetic clips. It also reports manually retaining 13K object images across 85 categories for synthetic generation.

license.media: Unnamed online video sources plus FLUX, Gemini, and Wan-generated derivatives
license.notes: Neither the mined media nor synthetic derivatives have published dataset-level license, attribution, commercial-use, or redistribution terms.

known_limitations: Online source platforms, URLs, licenses, collection dates, consent checks, and filtering retention by stage are not disclosed.
The synthetic component inherits limitations from FLUX, Gemini reference generation, FLUX Kontext, and Wan2.2-I2V.
Human-object categories and motions remain imbalanced despite synthetic supplementation.

processing.recipe: recipes/video_text
processing.notes: Preserve source URL and rights, person and object references, pose and segmentation outputs, action timeline, real-versus-synthetic flag, every generator version and seed, and filter decisions.

datasets.name: WorldWeaver Minecraft 126h
datasets.description: A paper-described corpus of synchronized two-agent Minecraft interactions with egocentric video, semantic controller inputs, physical agent state, a shared overhead camera, and generated scene-text supervision for world-state learning.

access.notes: The paper documents collection and annotation, but the authors have not published dataset files, a download process, or dataset-specific terms.

scale.notes: The paper reports approximately 126 synchronized hours at 832x480 and 20 FPS; it does not publish episode or clip counts, so no derived sample count is asserted here.

license.media: Not published; Minecraft and generated-annotation dependencies require review
license.notes: CC-BY-4.0 applies to the paper, not automatically to unreleased data; no dataset license or Minecraft asset-rights grant is stated.

known_limitations: Files and collection code are unavailable, so episode distribution, duplicates, corruption, and reported duration cannot be independently audited.
The corpus covers two-agent Minecraft sessions and may not transfer to real-world agents, photorealistic scenes, more players, or different action spaces.
Scene text is generated offline by Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct and can inherit hallucinations or miss state changes despite conditioning on synchronized views and actions.
The paper does not publish safety filtering, participant or server diversity, or dataset-specific usage terms.

processing.notes: Preserve all three synchronized camera streams, 20-Hz state and controller logs, and the four-frame scene-text alignment if files are released; do not infer missing counts from duration alone.

datasets.name: SANA-Video 2.0 Progressive Training Pools
datasets.description: The unreleased, progressively filtered image-video training collection described for SANA-Video 2.0, separated into broad pretraining, stricter continual-training, and small trusted supervised-fine-tuning pools.

access.notes: The paper reports aggregate stage scales and curation methods, but NVIDIA has not published media, metadata, manifests, or an application path.

scale.notes: The 5B production recipe reports about 30M pretraining clips, 10M continual-training clips, and 10K supervised-fine-tuning clips. The pools may be nested or overlapping, so they are not summed; 30M records the largest disclosed stage.

license.media: Proprietary in-house media pool; source identities and rights are not disclosed
license.notes: The paper's publication license and repository license do not license the underlying training media or generated annotations.

known_limitations: Source dataset names, collection dates, media rights, and per-source mixture shares are not published.
The report does not establish whether the 30M, 10M, and 10K stage pools are disjoint, nested, or partially overlapping.
Image batches are interleaved during joint training, but their counts, sources, and sampling cadence are not quantified.

processing.recipe: recipes/video_text
processing.notes: Reproductions should preserve raw provenance, shot boundaries, all independent filter scores, caption and motion-description model versions, stage membership, resolution, frame rate, and duration.

datasets.name: SANA-Video 2.0 Preference Pairs
datasets.description: The unreleased generated-video comparison data used for SANA-Video 2.0 Diffusion-DPO, with Gemini ranking candidates across fidelity, prompt alignment, motion quality, and temporal coherence.

access.notes: NVIDIA describes the ranking and unreliable-pair filtering recipe but publishes no prompts, candidates, pair records, rankings, or download request.

scale.notes: The report does not disclose the number of prompts, candidate videos, retained comparisons, or optimization samples.

license.media: Generated videos with undisclosed model and prompt provenance
license.notes: Neither the preference records nor dataset-specific licensing and redistribution terms have been released.

known_limitations: Gemini configuration, scoring prompts, agreement thresholds, and unreliable-ranking rejection rates are not disclosed.
An automated judge can introduce model-specific preferences and does not substitute for independently published human evaluation.
The later online ReFL reward stream is not a fixed downloadable dataset and is excluded from the pair count.

processing.notes: A reproducible release should retain prompt IDs, candidate seeds and checkpoint versions, all per-axis judge outputs, pair-filter decisions, and the exact Diffusion-DPO split.

datasets.name: Oxygen-TryOn Training Corpus
datasets.description: The unreleased image and try-on-triplet corpus used for Oxygen-TryOn continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning, built from real e-commerce, open-domain fashion, and model-generated images.

access.notes: The paper describes the data engine but publishes no files, manifest, request path, or retained-sample count.

scale.notes: More than 50M raw images enter filtering; retained image and triplet counts and the inherited general-purpose corpus size are not disclosed.
